target_year_over_year_context.explanation:
Both disclosures establish the segment reporting framework, stating that information is consistent with the chief operating decision maker's view and identifying the existence of four reportable business units.

Both disclosures define the Compute and Networking Business Unit (CNBU) and the specific markets it serves (data center/PC/graphics/networking vs client/cloud server/enterprise/graphics/networking), representing the same underlying segment entity.

Both disclosures define the Mobile Business Unit (MBU) and its focus on smartphone and mobile-device markets.

Both disclosures define the Embedded Business Unit (EBU) and its focus on automotive, industrial, and consumer markets (intelligent edge).

Both disclosures define the Storage Business Unit (SBU) and its focus on SSDs/component-level solutions for enterprise/cloud and consumer markets.

previous_disclosures.summary: The company identifies four reportable business units: Compute and Networking (CNBU), Mobile (MBU), Embedded (EBU), and Storage (SBU), each comprising specific memory, storage, and networking products for defined markets.

current_disclosures.summary: Segment information is consistent with how it is reviewed and evaluated by the chief operating decision maker, with four reportable business units identified.
The Compute and Networking Business Unit includes memory products and solutions sold into the data center, PC, graphics, and networking markets.
The Mobile Business Unit includes memory and storage products sold into the smartphone and other mobile-device markets.
The Embedded Business Unit includes memory and storage products and solutions sold into the intelligent edge through the automotive, industrial, and consumer embedded markets.
The Storage Business Unit includes SSDs and component-level storage solutions sold into the data center, PC, and consumer markets.

peer_results.rationale: No candidate was substantively comparable regarding a mobile segment definition. AMD's reportable segments (Data Center, Client, Gaming, Embedded) do not include a distinct 'Mobile' segment or disclose memory/storage products for smartphone markets in the provided text, whereas MU's disclosure specifically defines a Mobile Business Unit for such products.

comparisons.peer_summary: The semiconductor solutions segment provides devices for data center, service provider, and enterprise networking applications, including AI networking, as well as products for mobile, set-top box, broadband access, storage, industrial, and automotive markets. The segment also includes IP licensing.
comparisons.comparison: Both MU and AVGO disclose segments or business units that include specific offerings for mobile markets. MU's Mobile Business Unit (MBU) is defined as including memory and storage products sold into the smartphone and other mobile-device markets. Similarly, AVGO's Semiconductor Solutions segment explicitly provides products for mobile applications, including radio frequency devices, wireless connectivity, and touch controllers, while also covering data center and networking. Both disclose the inclusion of mobile-specific product lines within their broader segment definitions.

sentences.text: Mobile Business Unit ("MBU"): Includes memory and storage products sold into the smartphone and other mobile-device markets.
We provide a broad variety of radio frequency semiconductor devices, wireless connectivity solutions, custom touch controllers, and inductive charging solutions for mobile applications.

comparisons.peer_summary: The 'all other' category includes results from non-reportable segments such as Altera and Mobileye, start-up businesses supporting Intel initiatives, and historical results from divested businesses.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies address the composition of their reporting segments in the context of mobile-related businesses. MU explicitly defines a Mobile Business Unit (MBU) for smartphone markets. INTC includes the Mobileye business within its 'all other' non-reportable segment category. While MU treats mobile as a primary reportable unit, INTC aggregates mobile (via Mobileye) and other non-core/divested entities into a catch-all category, highlighting a difference in how mobile exposure is structured and reported.
